Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (four prior commits landed and clean: 9f46912, ab04241, 6631e05, b16298e). Build mode. This is SFCC-91 Step 4 of 4, the FINAL step: wiring the already-built `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` into `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — the only uncommitted file, +18/-0.

## Orchestrator's verdict (already run)

**IN SCOPE.** Exactly one file, two hunks (the import at line 75, the prop at lines 906-920), matching the plan's two permitted changes exactly. Verified by hunk-boundary line-range analysis, not just visual inspection, that neither of the two other `<ProductView>` call sites (lines 804, 830 — the set/bundle container and its child-product map) falls inside either changed hunk. All existing props on the modified (third, main) instance present, unmodified, same order. All hard-stop paths (product-view/index.tsx, the ZimmColourSwatchGroup/ZimmColourSwatch folders, any hook, theme/foundation, translations) confirmed zero diff. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Tester's findings (already run — very thorough, traced claims to real SDK type definitions and base SFCC reference mock fixtures rather than accepting the plan's framing)

**Gates, reproduced directly, all matching the stated baseline exactly:** tsc 0 errors; test 28 files/432 tests all passing; lint 20/4/16 exit 1, none of the 5 pre-existing warnings in this file fall on the new lines; audit:tokens 4/22 exit 1 unchanged, none attributable to this diff.

**Type coercions — confirmed necessary, but NOT equally safe, correcting an over-broad claim in my own launch brief.** Traced both fields to the real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` generated types (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:32297-32324`): `VariationAttributeValue.value: string` is REQUIRED with a documented min-length of 1 — `v.value ?? ''` can never fire on real data, fully safe. But `VariationAttribute.name?: string` (the attribute itself, not the value) is genuinely optional at the SDK contract level, no min-length guarantee — `attr.name ?? ''` protects against a real, SDK-documented possibility: a colour attribute with no display name would render the group label as a bare `":"`. Confirmed this exact case (`label=""`) is not exercised anywhere in `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own test suite (its test helper always hardcodes `label="Colour"`). 🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE, not proven to occur with Zimmermann's real catalog data (no live-API access this round to confirm either way), but a real, untested gap in the type contract's edge case.

**The `imageUrl` fallback — confirmed correct, with a citation correction.** My own launch brief claimed this chain matches `getVariantValueSwatch`'s own resolution; Tester found that function doesn't contain the fallback at all — it just returns the raw image object. The actual `disBaseLink || link` fallback the diff mirrors lives in the CONSUMER of that value, `product-view/index.tsx:716` (verbatim from base SFCC, already extracted and committed in Step 1). The diff's version matches that consuming logic exactly, correctly adding `?.` since it now runs unconditionally over all values (unlike base's guarded ternary). No defect — my citation was imprecise, the code itself is right.

**`attr.id === 'color'` — confirmed correct and internally consistent**, matching the identical literal already used in `product-view/index.tsx:740`'s `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` (Step 1) for the exact same shape decision.

**🟡 The substantive finding — a real scope-boundary gap in the PLAN's own reasoning, not a defect in this diff's conformance to that plan.** The plan (written earlier this build) excluded BOTH other `<ProductView>` instances (line 804 container, line 830 child-map) as "child products in a different layout, out of scope." Tester traced this against base SFCC's own reference mock fixtures (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/product-set-winter-lookM.js`, `product-bundle.js`):
- Line 804 (the set/bundle container itself): CONFIRMED has no top-level `variationAttributes` at all in either mock. This half of the exclusion is correct.
- Line 830 (each set/bundle CHILD product, rendered via its own full `<ProductView>`): CONFIRMED these are NOT read-only summaries — the mock's embedded child ("Quilted Jacket") carries a real, populated `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', name: 'Colour', values: [...]}]`, and `product-bundle.js` shows the identical shape 24+ times. Because this instance doesn't receive `renderVariationAttribute`, any such child's colour attribute falls through to the OLD unstyled base circular swatch rendering — on the same page where the main product now shows the NEW styled `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`. Tester could not confirm whether Zimmermann's actual live catalog currently has any set/bundle with colour-variant children (no live API/BM access this round) — the code path is proven real and reachable in generic SFCC data, not confirmed as currently live in this specific catalog.

**Also flagged, both non-blocking suggestions:** (1) `product-detail/index.tsx` has an established precedent — `selectPdpProductInfo`/`selectVariantScopedPriceData` — for extracting otherwise-untestable page-level SFCC-payload-to-view-model mapping into pure functions with their own `.test.ts`. The 4-line `attr → ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps` mapping in this diff is exactly that shape and currently has zero test coverage, direct or transitive (confirmed via grep — no test file imports this page's `./index` at all). The plan didn't require a test here and Tester agrees the branching itself needs none, but flags the mapping as a reasonable candidate for the same treatment. (2) `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s own scope is `overrides/app/components/**` + `overrides/app/theme/components/**` only — it never scans `overrides/app/pages/**` — moot for this specific diff (zero styling literals in it) but a pre-existing, codebase-wide gap for any future page-level styling.

**What Tester could not verify (structural, not a gap in effort):** any actual rendered output (no dev-server/browser access this round); AC 4 (URL updates without full reload) — mechanically wired correctly (href flows straight into ZimmColourSwatch's react-router Link, same mechanism as base), but genuinely requires a real browser, exactly as the plan already defers to Marcel's own dev-server check; whether Zimmermann's live catalog has any bundle/set with colour-variant children today.

## Your job

Score against your six axes and return PASS or REWORK. The central judgement call: does the set/bundle-child finding belong to THIS step's Correctness/Completeness (i.e., does Step 4 need rework to also wire the line-830 instance), or is it a real discovery that sits outside SFCC-91's own stated scope (the ticket and its ACs are entirely about the standalone PDP; nothing in it mentions bundles or sets) and should instead be surfaced to Marcel as a follow-up finding rather than actioned inside this story? Weigh Hard Rule 5/"never expand scope" against the real, user-visible inconsistency this creates. State your reasoning explicitly, not just the verdict. Also state plainly whether this step, once your verdict is settled, is ready for Marcel's own dev-server visual check (the plan's designated final gate for AC 4 and the four other items nothing automated can verify) or whether anything else needs to happen first.

swatch's outward-drawn outline had its right edge painted over by the
next sibling's opaque background - normal document flow paints later
siblings on top, and neither element had a stacking context of its own.
zIndex alone is empirically sufficient for a flex item per spec, but
position: relative is kept too so the rule holds if this component is

variation attribute, leaving the others on the base markup. Mirrors the

## Six-axis review — SFCC-91 Step 4/4 (wiring `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` into `product-detail/index.tsx`)

I read the actual diff directly, re-derived the Orchestrator's and Tester's key claims from source rather than accepting them, and ran the gates myself.

| Axis | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | No dev-server/browser access this round (same constraint the Tester hit). Static trace shows correct wiring, but per this repo's own rule, rendered-output correctness cannot be inferred from green gates — it needs the visual checkpoint. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | ACs 1/2/3/5 are provably satisfied by tracing the prop mapping into `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own (already-tested) branch logic. AC 4 (URL-without-reload) is mechanically correct (`href` flows into the same react-router `Link` mechanism already proven elsewhere) but its full confirmation is explicitly a browser-only check, deferred by the plan to Marcel's own dev-server pass — that's the plan's design, not a gap in this diff. No new component needed a story/test here — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already has both from Step 3. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator's verdict is IN SCOPE, not UNDER — that's the axis's evidence per my brief. See judgement call below for why I did not override this. |
| **Correctness** | PASS | Independently reproduced: `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors. `npx vitest run` → 28 files / 432 tests, all green. `npx pwa-kit-dev lint` on this file → 5 warnings at lines 183, 183, 313, 322, 360 — all pre-existing, none on the new lines (75, 906–920). `npx prettier --check` clean. No 🔴 findings from either agent or from my own trace. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | Relative import (`'../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup'`) matches the file's own existing pattern (`zimmProductMeta`, `product-view`) and doesn't fall under overrideStyling.md's base-path rule (that rule governs re-importing an *already-overridden SFCC* component; `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` has no SFCC base equivalent). Zero styling literals in the diff. `npm run audit:tokens` → same 4 pre-existing unacknowledged violations, none in this diff's file (the tool doesn't even scan `pages/**`, and there's nothing to scan here regardless — verified by reading the diff). |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | Diff is exactly the import + the `renderVariationAttribute` callback on the one permitted `<ProductView>` instance, matching the plan's two hunks. |

**Overall: PASS** (five axes hold; Design fidelity is UNVERIFIED, pending the plan's own designated dev-server gate — not a defect in the work).

---

## The central judgement call: does the set/bundle-child gap belong to Step 4?

I independently re-derived the Tester's finding from source, not just their citation, before deciding:

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:62-70` (`normalizeSetBundleProduct`) confirms `childProducts[n].product` for a **set** is a deep clone of the raw `setProducts[n]` entry, verbatim — including its top-level `variationAttributes`. For a **bundle**, `bundledProducts[n]` is spread the same way.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/product-set-winter-lookM.js:377-384` shows a real child ("Quilted Jacket") with `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', name: 'Colour', values: [{name: 'royal', ..., value: 'JJ5FUXX'}]}, ...]` at exactly that top level. `product-bundle.js` has 23 occurrences of `id: 'color'` in the same shape (Tester said "24+" — immaterial rounding, the phenomenon is real either way).
- `product-detail/index.tsx:830`'s `<ProductView>` call does not receive `renderVariationAttribute`, so `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` (product-view/index.tsx:866) falls through to the old unstyled circular-swatch rendering for any such child.

**So the finding is real and CONFIRMED, not speculative.** The question is what to do with it.

I'm treating this as **out of Step 4's scope, to be surfaced as a follow-up, not reworked here**, for four reasons:

1. **The plan already made this call before implementation**, excluding both other `<ProductView>` instances as "child products in a different layout, out of scope." Step 4's diff is faithful to that plan — it didn't discover the gap and paper over it, the gap was a pre-existing plan decision.
2. **The Orchestrator's job is specifically scope verification**, and it certified IN SCOPE — explicitly checking that lines 804/830 fall outside the changed hunks as the *intended* boundary, not as an oversight it missed. Restraint's evidence source (per my brief) is that verdict.
3. **SFCC-91's own ACs (per this task's framing) are standalone-PDP only** — nothing in the ticket mentions bundles or sets. There is no unmet AC for *this* ticket.
4. **Actually fixing it here would be a bigger problem than leaving it**, not a smaller one: passing the same `renderVariationAttribute` callback into the line-830 instance would render `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in a layout context (a set/bundle child column) that no Figma node has been confirmed for. That's not a safe "just wire it up" — it's a new, undesigned UI decision dressed as a bug fix, which would fail Design fidelity for real (an unconfirmed rendering) rather than leave it honestly unverified. AGENTS.md's Minimal-changes rule ("propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently") and Hard Rule 5 both point the same direction: this is a decision for Marcel, not something to resolve unilaterally inside this gate three reviews deep.

Weighed against Hard Rule 5/restraint: expanding Step 4 to cover line 830 would itself be the scope violation — done without a plan update, without confirming a Figma treatment exists for that context, and overriding both the plan's own prior decision and the Orchestrator's already-issued scope verdict. The correct action is to **not** REWORK this step, and instead flag the finding loudly for Marcel to decide: file a follow-up (either its own ticket, e.g. "wire colour swatches for set/bundle children," or an AC amendment to SFCC-91 if Marcel judges it belongs there) — including asking whether a Figma treatment for that context exists at all before anyone builds it.

**A second, smaller instance of the same "inherited-not-introduced" pattern**, found independently rather than from the Tester's list: `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:32297-32312` shows the real SDK's `VariationAttributeValue.name` is *also* optional (`name?: string`), while the local `SfccVariationValue` type in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:99` (`name: string`, required, no `?`) already treats it as guaranteed — a Step 1 typing decision, not a Step 4 one. The Step 4 diff's `name: v.name` (line 914) just passes that field straight through into `ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps.values[].name: string`, consistent with the type contract Step 1 already established and already committed. Fixing the type would mean editing `product-view/index.tsx`, a file this step is required to leave at zero diff — out of bounds here for the same Hard-Rule-5 reason as the finding above. CONFIRMED, informational, worth folding into the same follow-up conversation, not a Step 4 blocker.

---

## What I tried to falsify

- Reproduced `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest run`, `pwa-kit-dev lint` (scoped to this file), `prettier --check`, and `audit:tokens` myself rather than trusting the reported numbers — all matched exactly, including the specific line numbers of pre-existing lint warnings being untouched by this diff.
- Traced every field in the prop-mapping object (`value`, `name`, `href`, `imageUrl`) back through the local `SfccVariationAttribute`/`SfccVariationValue` types in `product-view/index.tsx` and cross-checked those against the real generated SDK types in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` — found one additional inherited (not new) type-looseness the Tester hadn't listed (`v.name` optional at the SDK level vs. required locally).
- Went past the Tester's citation of the set/bundle mock fixtures and read the actual normalization code (`normalizeSetBundleProduct`) myself to confirm the data-flow claim mechanically, not just at the fixture level — confirmed a set/bundle child's `variationAttributes` really does survive unmodified into what `<ProductView>` at line 830 receives.
- Checked whether the new import violates the "already-overridden component" relative-path rule — it doesn't, since `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` has no SFCC base counterpart.
- Checked for a Completeness gap on the mapping logic itself (no dedicated test) against the codebase's own precedent (`productInfo.ts`/`variantScopedPrice.ts`) — confirmed the precedent is real and the gap exists, but judged it a reasonable non-blocking suggestion given the mapping has no branching testing.md's bar is aimed at, consistent with the Tester's own framing.
- Checked the empty-string degenerate case of `v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link` against `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `Boolean(value.imageUrl)` filter — confirmed it still correctly filters out, no gap.

## What I could not verify

- **Design fidelity** — no dev-server/browser access. UNVERIFIED, not passed.
- **AC 4 in a real browser** — mechanism is correct by inspection, but "updates without full reload" is a runtime claim I can't execute here.
- **Whether Zimmermann's live catalog currently has any set/bundle with colour-variant children** — no live API/Business Manager access this round, same gap the Tester hit. The code path is proven reachable in generic SFCC data (independently, via the base mocks), not confirmed live in this specific catalog today.

## Findings (none blocking — all informational)

- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:906-920` — set/bundle child products with a populated colour attribute will render the base default swatch UI, not `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, on the same page as the newly-styled main product. **CONFIRMED** (independently traced through `product-utils.js`'s normalization and the base mock fixtures). Not a Step 4 defect — out of SFCC-91's stated scope per the plan and the Orchestrator's scope verdict. Instruction: raise as a follow-up item for Marcel to scope (new ticket vs. AC amendment), and check whether a Figma treatment for that layout context exists before anyone implements it.
- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:99` (`SfccVariationValue.name: string`) — looser at the real SDK contract (`name?: string`) than the local type admits. **CONFIRMED** against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:32297`. Inherited from Step 1, out of Step 4's zero-diff scope for that file. Instruction: fold into the same follow-up conversation, not a Step 4 fix.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:906-920` mapping logic has no dedicated test, unlike the page's own `selectPdpProductInfo`/`selectVariantScopedPriceData` precedent. **CONFIRMED** (no test imports this page's `./index` at all). Non-blocking suggestion only, per Tester's own framing and testing.md's "non-obvious or costly to debug" bar.

## Is this ready for Marcel's dev-server visual check?

**Yes — nothing else needs to happen first.** Every gate that can run without a browser has been independently reproduced clean, the diff is minimal and matches its two permitted hunks exactly, and the one open finding (set/bundle children) is a scope question for Marcel to route, not a defect blocking this step's own deliverable.
